meta.stem: Failed RSI. Facial trauma. Videolaryngoscopy twice. i-gel not ventilating. SpO2 68%. You are the AED doctor. The manikin, the nurse, and the airway trolley are in the bay.
meta.guidelineNotes:
Scoring truth is this AW-EM-01 script, updated to DAS 2025 (Br J Anaesth 2025; 136: 283–307). The kit card is scalpel–bougie–tube: scalpel, bougie, lubricated cuffed 6.0 mm tube. DAS 2025 drops the 2015 choice between a stab and a cut-down: every patient gets a midline vertical skin incision, up to 8 cm, bottom to top, then finger dissection down to the membrane. The steps after that (transverse stab with the cutting edge toward you, rotate 90° so the sharp edge points to the feet, swap hands and pull the blade toward you, coudé bougie 10–15 cm, railroad the 6.0 rotating, cuff up, capnography) follow the DAS scalpel–bougie–tube sequence. The full 2025 text was paywalled when this pack was written; check the step detail against it.

Your own source notes describe the older ATLS-style teaching station (number 11 blade, tracheal hook, Trousseau dilator). That belongs in a separate teaching station, not this CICO resus.

Rocuronium 1.2 mg/kg is the scripted dose if the patient is not fully relaxed. DAS says ensure neuromuscular blockade before front-of-neck access and does not print 1.2 mg/kg on the algorithm card. The dose is kept as written.

This station starts after a failed RSI. Etomidate and suxamethonium are not on the trolley and are not scored.

In the bench, SpO2 keeps falling from 68% until the lungs are ventilated through the trachea; below 45% he arrests. Each run randomises the neck (slim, or obese with an impalpable membrane) and whether the bougie finds a false passage. An early bougie hold-up is a false tract: forcing it and ventilating it does not produce ETCO2. Needle-first is not the adult plan while a scalpel is on the trolley. A child is an ENT plus needle algorithm, not an adult 6.0 hole.

marks.label: Declare can't-intubate can't-oxygenate and start front-of-neck access
Call for help immediately
Name the AED consultant
Name anaesthetics
Name ENT
Name ICU and say a surgical airway is starting
Keep 100% oxygen on the i-gel or mask
Rocuronium 1.2 mg/kg now if not fully relaxed
Number-10 scalpel, bougie, and a lubricated cuffed 6.0
Maximum neck extension; stand on the patient's left if right-handed
Laryngeal handshake
Say the landmarks: thyroid, membrane, cricoid in the midline — or that the membrane is impalpable
Midline vertical skin incision up to 8 cm, bottom to top, then finger dissection to the membrane
Non-dominant hand never leaves the larynx
Transverse stab through the membrane, cutting edge toward you
Rotate the blade 90 degrees, sharp edge toward the feet
Swap hands and pull the blade laterally so the hole stays open
Coudé bougie 10–15 cm; early hold-up means a false tract
Railroad a 6.0, cuff just through the membrane, bougie out, cuff up, circuit on
Ask for a square ETCO2 waveform before calling it success
No ETCO2: tube out, still CICO, do not ventilate a false tract
Hold the tube until it is tied and a named person takes it; depth is short, not 22 cm
Chest X-ray; keep the patient paralysed and sedated
ISBAR to ENT and ICU; family after the cut; document the times
Viva: not needle-first in an adult; 6.0 fits the membrane; paralysis helps; a collar does not cancel the knife; a child is not an adult hole

actions.hint: Say it out loud: this is CICO. Front-of-neck access now.

options.label: This is CICO. Front-of-neck access now.
options.detail: You: This is can't-intubate, can't-oxygenate. I am declaring CICO. Front-of-neck access now.

options.label: One more look with the videolaryngoscope
options.detail: SpO2 is 68% and the i-gel is dead. Another videolaryngoscopy is not front-of-neck access.

options.label: A quick history before anyone cuts
options.detail: There is no time for a history. Oxygen stays on and you declare CICO.

actions.hint: Tell the nurse to call for help. A surgical airway is starting.

options.label: Call for help now. CICO, surgical airway starting.
options.detail: Nurse: Calling. I will only call the people you name.

options.label: Wait for ENT to arrive before any cut
options.detail: You have declared CICO. Waiting for ENT before the scalpel is a delay.

actions.hint: Name the AED consultant, anaesthetics, ENT, and ICU.

options.label: AED consultant
options.detail: Nurse: AED consultant.

options.label: Anaesthetics
options.detail: Nurse: Anaesthetics.

options.label: ENT
options.detail: Nurse: ENT.

options.label: ICU — tell them CICO, surgical airway starting
options.detail: Nurse: ICU knows a surgical airway is starting.

actions.hint: Use the phone if you have not already named the teams.

options.label: AED consultant
Anaesthetics
ENT
ICU — CICO, surgical airway starting
Psychiatry
options.detail: Psychiatry is not the team for a surgical airway.

options.label: Ask for another videolaryngoscope instead
options.detail: Another videolaryngoscope is the critical miss. You need a scalpel.

actions.hint: Leave 100% oxygen on the i-gel or the mask.

options.label: 100% oxygen stays on the i-gel. No history.
options.detail: You: Keep 100% oxygen on the i-gel. Do not take a history.

options.label: Take the i-gel out and look again
options.detail: You have lost the oxygen route and you still have not cut.

actions.hint: If the patient is not fully relaxed, give rocuronium 1.2 mg/kg now.

options.label: Fully relaxed? If not, rocuronium 1.2 mg/kg now.
options.detail: You: Full relaxant in? If not, rocuronium 1.2 mg/kg now.

options.label: Let the paralysis wear off, then look
options.detail: A moving larynx makes front-of-neck access harder. You need paralysis, then the scalpel.

actions.hint: Walk to the airway trolley. Number-10 scalpel, bougie, lubricated cuffed 6.0.

options.label: Number-10 scalpel
Bougie
Lubricated cuffed 6.0
Needle cricothyroidotomy set only
options.detail: A scalpel is on the trolley. Needle-only is not the adult plan.

options.label: One more videolaryngoscope blade
options.detail: The third look is the critical miss.

options.label: Tracheal hook, and leave the bougie
options.detail: This card is scalpel-bougie-tube. The hook is a different kit.

actions.hint: Or tell the nurse to bring the number-10 scalpel, the bougie, and a 6.0.
actions.prompt: Ask the nurse for the kit

options.label: Number-10 scalpel, bougie, lubricated cuffed 6.0.
options.detail: Nurse: Scalpel, bougie, and a 6.0 are in your hand.

actions.hint: Scalpel–bougie–tube: extend, handshake, vertical midline incision, finger to the membrane, stab, turn, bougie, 6.0, capnography.

options.label: Scalpel–bougie–tube, now.
options.detail: The front-of-neck airway is done.
options.performHint: Do it as you would on a real patient: position, find the larynx, cut, stab, open, bougie, tube, confirm. SpO2 keeps falling until you ventilate through the trachea. Nothing stops a mistake; the debrief shows what to fix.

options.label: I am not going to cut
options.detail: SpO2 is 68%. Never cutting is the critical miss.

options.label: Needle only. The scalpel stays on the trolley.
options.detail: The scalpel is on the trolley. Needle-only in this adult is the wrong plan.

options.label: Advance the tube to 22 cm at the skin
options.detail: A front-of-neck tube is short at the skin. 22 cm is an oral-tube depth.

options.label: Bag it. I don't need a waveform.
options.detail: No ETCO2. Do not celebrate, and do not keep ventilating a tract you have not confirmed.

actions.hint: You hold the tube until it is tied and someone named takes it. Depth is short. Then a chest X-ray, and stay paralysed and sedated.

options.label: Chest X-ray. Stay paralysed and sedated.
options.detail: Chest X-ray is ordered. Paralysis and sedation continue.

options.label: Let go, the tie can wait
options.detail: A front-of-neck tube falls out. You hold it until it is secured.

actions.hint: ISBAR to ENT and ICU. Family after the cut, not before. Document the times.

options.label: ISBAR: CICO, surgical airway, ETCO2, convert when stable, ICU bed.
options.detail: You: CICO after failed RSI, facial trauma, SpO2 was 68%. Scalpel-bougie-tube, square ETCO2, tube held and tied. Please convert when stable and take an ICU bed. Family are told after the cut, not before. Times are in the notes.

options.label: Phone the family before I cut
options.detail: The family are told after the airway is in, not before the scalpel.

actions.hint: If the examiner asks: needle, tube size, paralysis, collar, and the child.

options.label: Why scalpel, not needle, in this adult?
options.detail: Needle-first fails too often in adults. A scalpel is on the trolley, so the plan is scalpel-bougie-tube. A 6.0 fits the cricothyroid membrane. Paralysis makes the larynx still enough to cut. A collar does not cancel the knife. A child goes to ENT and a needle algorithm, not an adult 6.0 hole.

options.label: No ETCO2 after the tube. What now?
options.detail: You: No ETCO2 means the tube is not in the trachea. Tube out, still CICO. Finger into the hole, bougie under the finger, 6.0 again. Never ventilate a tract you have not confirmed.

options.label: Needle first. A scalpel is too much.
options.detail: That is the adult critical miss when a scalpel is already on the trolley.

options.label: Same adult 6.0 hole in a 4-year-old
options.detail: An adult surgical hole and a 6.0 is the wrong operation in a toddler. Call ENT and use the needle algorithm.

sequenceRules.failNote: The scalpel came out before you declared CICO.

sequenceRules.okNote: Scalpel, bougie, and 6.0 were named before the cut.
sequenceRules.failNote: You cut before the DAS kit was in your hand.
